title: Open restriction of a smooth projective strict normal crossings pair
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $R$ be a smooth projective $F$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective], and let $E\subseteq R$ be a reduced relative strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Thus it is an effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with finitely many distinct integral components $E_i$, each smooth over $F$ of codimension one, and every intersection of $r$ distinct components is empty or smooth over $F$ of pure codimension $r$. Suppose also that $R$ is regular, $E$ is a strict normal crossings boundary on $R$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], and at every point the equations of its components through that point are distinct members of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $U\subseteq R$ be any open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $U$ is smooth over $F$ and admits a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $F$. The restriction $E_U=E\times_R U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is reduced and effective Cartier. Its distinct integral irreducible components are exactly the nonempty $E_i\times_R U$, and the intersection indexed by $J$ is $(\bigcap_{i\in J}E_i)\times_R U$, smooth over $F$ of pure codimension $|J|$ whenever nonempty. At $u\in U$ the canonical isomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,u}\cong\mathcal O_{R,u}$ identifies all component ideals and their regular-parameter equations. The scheme $U$ is regular and $E_U$ is a strict normal crossings boundary on $U$. These assertions include $U=\varnothing$, $E=\varnothing$ and the empty index subset $J$, whose intersection is $U$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-open-immersion], $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_R|_U$. At $u\in U$, sending a representative $(V,s)$ to $(V\cap U,s|_{V\cap U})$ identifies germs on $R$ with germs on $U$: conversely an open neighbourhood of $u$ in $U$ is already open in $R$, with the same sections. The two maps are inverse, since restriction does not change a germ. This gives the canonical local ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,u}\cong\mathcal O_{R,u}$, as rings with their maximal ideals. The same argument applies to every open subscheme used below.

Apply [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] to $U\hookrightarrow R$ and the given smooth structure map $R\to\operatorname{Spec}F$. It gives that $U\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is smooth. More generally, if $T$ is any one of the smooth intersections $E_J=\bigcap_{i\in J}E_i$ appearing in [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor], the open subscheme $T\cap U\hookrightarrow T$ is smooth over $F$ by the same lemma. This includes the empty intersection $E_\varnothing=R$.

By [def-kun-projective] choose a closed immersion $i:R\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf P^N_F$ with $N$ finite. The subset $i(R\setminus U)$ is closed in $P$: $R\setminus U$ is closed in $R$, and $i$ is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $W=P\setminus i(R\setminus U)$. Then $i^{-1}(W)=U$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction] to $i$ and the open $W$; it gives a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow W$. Composing with $W\hookrightarrow P$ is a locally closed immersion, by the immersion definition in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. These maps are over $F$, since they are restrictions of $i$.

proof.text: For each closed subscheme $T\hookrightarrow R$ among $E$, the $E_i$, and their intersections, apply clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction]. Its restriction is a closed subscheme $T\cap U\hookrightarrow U$ with exactly the restricted ideal sheaf. It represents $T\times_R U$: a pair of maps to $T$ and $U$ over $R$ has its unique map into $T$ landing in the open preimage of $U$, and hence factors uniquely through this open subscheme. This verifies the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product]. In particular $E_U$ and $E_{i,U}$ are these open subschemes. On an open $V\subseteq U$ the ambient rings and all these defining ideals are literally their values on the same open $V\subseteq R$; on stalks they correspond under step 1.

source.place: Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); schemes.tex Tag 01IO (definition-immersion); more-morphisms.tex Tag 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening), applied only to the underlying closed immersion

proof.text: The local rings of $E_U$, as an open subscheme of $E$, are those of $E$ by step 1; they are reduced, so $E_U$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The Cartier generator condition restricts directly: around $u\in U$ choose a Cartier chart $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq R$ with ideal $(f)$, $f$ a non-zero-divisor, and shrink to a principal open $D(g)\subseteq V\cap U$ containing $u$. In $A_g$, $f(a/g^n)=0$ implies $g^mfa=0$ for some $m$; cancellation of $f$ gives $g^ma=0$, hence $a/g^n=0$. Thus $f$ remains a non-zero-divisor and generates the restricted ideal on $D(g)$. These charts cover $U$, giving [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Finally, every nonempty affine open of a nonempty $E_{i,U}$ is an affine open of $E_i$ with the same ring, an integral domain. Therefore $E_{i,U}$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-irreducible-closed-correspondence] to the open subspace $|E_U|\subseteq|E|$. Its order-preserving bijection of irreducible closed subsets, with inverse closure, identifies the maximal ones with the components $|E_i|$ that meet $U$. Indeed the closure in $E$ of an irreducible closed subset of $E_U$ lies in some $E_i$: an irreducible set contained in a finite union of closed sets lies in one of them (induct on the number of closed sets using the definition of irreducibility). Maximality in either space is then equivalent by that order correspondence. Distinct surviving components remain distinct by injectivity. Step 5 already proves that their open subschemes are integral, hence reduced, so their scheme structures are the claimed integral component structures. They exhaust $E_U$ and are pairwise incomparable. For scheme-theoretic union use [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-union] repeatedly: its ideal-intersection formula on an affine open $V\subseteq U$ is identical to the formula on the same affine open of $R$, and the given equality $E=\bigcup_i E_i$ therefore restricts to $E_U=\bigcup_i E_{i,U}$. Empty members have unit ideal and can be removed.

proof.text: For any subset $J$ of the original component labels, $\bigcap_{i\in J}E_{i,U}=E_J\times_R U$. To check the identification, a map into either scheme is exactly a map into $U$ whose composite into $R$ factors through every $E_i$ for $i\in J$; uniqueness follows from the closed immersions being inclusions. This is the same fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Smoothness is step 2. For pure codimension use precisely the affine formulation of [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]: every affine open $V\subseteq U$ is an affine open of $R$ with the same ring and the same defining ideal of $E_J$ by step 4. Its minimal primes consequently have the same heights $|J|$ as before. This proves the pure codimension assertion with no dimension-of-open comparison. At $u\in U$ the component ideals correspond by step 4; the very same generators in the local ring remain distinct members of the same regular system of parameters under step 1, since its maximal ideal and Krull dimension are unchanged [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters].

source.place: Tags 01HF (example-open-subspace) and 01IO (definition-immersion); ILO Expose X, definition after Theorem 2.1, printed p.149; algebra.tex Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local)

proof.text: Finally use the regularity criterion in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The scheme $R$ and every $E_J$ are locally Noetherian with regular local rings, the latter assertions being part of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Their open restrictions remain locally Noetherian by the explicit open-subscheme assertion in [pqf-def-locnoeth], and have the same regular local rings by step 1. They are therefore regular. At every $u\in E_J\cap U$ both local rings in $\dim\mathcal O_{R,u}=\dim\mathcal O_{E_J,u}+|J|$ are unchanged, so the same equation holds for $U$ and $E_J\cap U$. The restricted ideal is radical directly as well: on any open $V\subseteq U$, it is the original ideal on the same open of $R$ by step 4, so $a^n$ in that ideal implies $a$ is in it by the original boundary hypothesis. Together with the reduced Cartier divisor of step 5 and its finite distinct integral components of step 6, these are exactly all clauses of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] for $E_U\subseteq U$. If $U$ is empty all pointwise conditions are vacuous and its immersion is the empty closed subscheme of $P$. If $E$ is empty its ideal is the unit ideal, generated by $1$, and it has no components. If $J=\varnothing$, both intersections are the ambient scheme and the codimension is zero. Thus none of the arguments imposes a nonemptiness hypothesis beyond the stated nonempty components.
